title: SARS spike-protein modification proposal rejected by DARPA, moved to Wuhan

tellings.quote: And in 2017, you have uh basically a modification of SARS, you know, that allows it, you know, with the spike protein to bind to human ACE2 receptors through the Ecoalth Alliance submitted to DARPA.

plain: In 2017, Michels says, EcoHealth Alliance, a US nonprofit research group, sent DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, a proposal to change a SARS virus so that its spike protein could attach to ACE2, a receptor on human cells, and when DARPA turned it down the work moved to the Wuhan Institute of Virology in China. Michels tells it himself on a 2025 episode with Brigham Buhler, naming Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the US health official Anthony Fauci, and draws on no named document. He raises it as a sign that the research behind the COVID virus may have been planned in the open and then moved abroad.
